clue.text: Swimsuit escape: Einstein thought about it a lot

definitions.text: Einstein thought about it a lot

parts.note: Speedo is a brand name for a close-fitting swimsuit
flight is the act of escaping or fleeing

explanation.surface: A puzzling pairing of beachwear, a getaway and a physicist's musings.
explanation.walkthrough: SPEEDO + FLIGHT re-spaced reads SPEED OF LIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: The constant c was central to Einstein's relativity work, so it occupied his thinking for years.

clue.text: Rustic, pastoral deity embracing humble mass

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so the outer word wraps its arms around the rest

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of shepherds and flocks
lowly, of modest rank
m is the abbreviation for mass

explanation.surface: A country god is pictured hugging the simple common people.
explanation.walkthrough: Humble mass looks like the peasantry, but it is two separate pieces placed inside PAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A plowman is a farm labourer who drives a plough, a typical country person; rustic is used as a noun here.

clue.text: Regime changes for expat

indicators.note: changes signals that the preceding word is rearranged into something new

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A change of government prompts someone to leave the country.
explanation.definitionFit: An émigré is a person who has left their own country to live abroad, as an expatriate does.

clue.text: Poet: "God is the connection"

indicators.note: the answer runs across the connection, the joins between neighbouring words

parts.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: A poet declares that the divine links everything together.
explanation.walkthrough: The quoted line looks like a poet's creed; the answer sits inside it, from the second letter of God to the first of the.
explanation.definitionFit: An odist is a writer of odes, a kind of poet.

clue.text: To make the rules, member misses the beginning

parts.note: a leg is a limb, which is a member of the body
someone who misses the start of an event is late for it

explanation.surface: A club member skips the opening of the meeting where the rules are drawn up.
explanation.walkthrough: Misses the beginning looks like an instruction to drop a first letter, but it is read as a phrase: someone who misses the beginning is late.
explanation.definitionFit: To legislate is to make laws, which are the rules of a state.

clue.text: Dangerous wave of gray engulfing most of a Middle Eastern capital

indicators.note: to engulf is to swallow up, so the outer word surrounds the other

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: most of means nearly all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Amman is the capital of Jordan

explanation.surface: A menacing grey sea swallows a Middle Eastern city.
explanation.walkthrough: Gray keeps its American spelling here, which matters: the city goes between its first letter and the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Gamma rays are high-energy electromagnetic radiation, a wave form harmful to living tissue.

clue.text: Well-behaved child is into fruit

indicators.note: the word into is split, and its first half says what comes next goes around

parts.note: the second half of the word into, taken as written
a good, obedient child is called a little angel

explanation.surface: A good child has developed a liking for fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Into looks like a single word meaning keen on, but it splits in two: in is the instruction and to supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangelo is a citrus fruit, a cross between a tangerine and a pomelo or grapefruit.

clue.text: Wasps sting bears, yo

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so the words carry the answer within them

parts.note: the letters span the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A warning shouted to someone that wasps sting.
explanation.definitionFit: Psst is a whispered call to catch someone's attention, just as yo is a call to get it.

clue.text: If Julius Caesar said this word, point outside

indicators.note: one item set outside another wraps around it, holding the other within

parts.note: a prong is a sharp point, as on a fork
Caesar's famous boast was veni, vidi, vici; vidi is Latin for I saw

explanation.surface: A cryptic instruction about Caesar's speech, which also contains the definition at its very start.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'If' reads as setting up a hypothetical, but it is the definition; the rest points to one word of Caesar's three-word boast.
explanation.definitionFit: Providing is a conjunction meaning on condition that, which is a synonym of if.

clue.text: Hundredth PC: "Enter" breaking down

indicators.note: something breaking down falls apart, so the letters are reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A personal computer's Enter key gives out on its hundredth press.
explanation.definitionFit: Percent means one part in a hundred, so one percent is a hundredth.

clue.text: -26, somehow

indicators.note: somehow says the letters arrive by some unstated rearrangement

parts.note: the answer to 26 across, IN SUM, supplies the letters

explanation.surface: It looks like a bare number with a minus sign, as if a sum were being set.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen before 26 is the definition: the sign itself is read aloud as the answer. 26 across is IN SUM, whose letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The printed sign for subtraction or a negative number is called minus.

clue.text: Alcohol as an alternative in dish

parts.note: rum is a spirit, a kind of alcohol
or is the word that offers an alternative

explanation.surface: A cook adds booze to a dish as a substitute ingredient.
explanation.walkthrough: Dish here is the American slang noun for gossip, not a plate of food. RUMOR is the American spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Dish is informal American for juicy gossip, and a rumor is a piece of such talk.

clue.text: Will state absurd theories, initially about guys

indicators.note: about means around, so the scrambled letters surround what follows
something absurd is nonsensical, so these letters are scrambled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the opening letter of theories
guys are men

explanation.surface: Someone called Will lays out ridiculous ideas about men.
explanation.walkthrough: Will is not a man's name but a legal document. Absurd works on state together with the first letter of theories.
explanation.definitionFit: A last will and testament is the legal document setting out how a person's estate is divided.

clue.text: Workers lacking leadership for billions of years

indicators.note: lacking leadership says the word loses its leader, its first letter

parts.note: peons are labourers, especially unskilled farm workers in Latin America

explanation.surface: A leaderless workforce has drifted for an eternity.
explanation.walkthrough: PEONS without its first letter leaves EONS.
explanation.definitionFit: An eon is an immense span of geological time, often a billion years, so eons are billions of years.

clue.text: Tangled tale: "Across and Down: ways to get there"

indicators.note: tangled things are knotted and jumbled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A muddled story claims crossword directions are routes to a destination.
explanation.walkthrough: Across and Down look like crossword labels; Across is fodder, and Down is part of the definition, since escalators carry people down as well as up.
explanation.definitionFit: Escalators are moving staircases, a means of travelling down or up between floors.

clue.text: Jobs at the bottom of the scale for a longshoreman

parts.note: Steve Jobs, co-founder of Apple

parts.words: at the bottom of the scale
parts.note: do and re are the two lowest notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: The lowest-paid jobs go to dock workers.
explanation.walkthrough: Jobs looks like employment but is the Apple founder's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore is a person who loads and unloads ships, the same work as a longshoreman.

clue.text: Present outside operating room — in closet, maybe

indicators.note: outside says one word sits around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: to stage a play is to present it
OR is the standard abbreviation for operating room

explanation.surface: A gift is hidden outside the hospital theatre, perhaps tucked into a cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: Present looks like a gift but is a verb, to put on a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Things kept in a closet are in storage, put away until needed; the closet is one example.

clue.text: Diversions from Pennsylvania's halfback holding tight end

indicators.note: holding means keeping something inside, so a letter is placed within

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania, plus the S of the possessive

indicators.note: 'end' keeps only the first letter of 'tight'

parts.note: the end letter of tight; tight end is also a position in American football
half is SEMI, and back turns it round

explanation.surface: An American football report on a Pennsylvania running back marking a tight end.
explanation.walkthrough: Halfback and tight end look like football positions. Halfback splits into half, the prefix semi, read back; together with the state, it then surrounds a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastimes are hobbies or recreations, activities that divert and amuse.

clue.text: Endangered, agitated teen interrupts online conversation

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so this goes inside

parts.note: a thread is a chain of posts in an online discussion

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so the word's letters are shaken into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A worried teenager barges into a chat because something is at risk.
explanation.walkthrough: Online conversation looks like a chat app, but it is the word for a chain of forum posts.
explanation.definitionFit: An endangered species or place is one under threat, so threatened is a synonym.

clue.text: Rise unsteadily and beg to publish again

indicators.note: unsteadily suggests wobbling, so the letters fall into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
to sue for something is to plead or petition for it

explanation.surface: Someone staggers to their feet and pleads for another print run.
explanation.walkthrough: The and simply joins the pieces; beg is the sense of sue in sue for peace.
explanation.definitionFit: To reissue a book is to issue it a second time, putting it back on sale.

clue.text: Say no to donut, following doctor

indicators.note: following places one piece after another in the build order

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor
a ring doughnut is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A dieter refuses a doughnut on medical advice.
explanation.walkthrough: The donut comes after the doctor, so VET comes first and O follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To veto something is to reject or forbid it, refusing it outright.

clue.text: Seize me from below with one type of blood blockage

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading from below means taking the letters bottom to top

parts.note: to grab is to seize
taken as written
O is one of the four main blood groups

explanation.surface: A medical plea about a blood clot attacking from below.
explanation.walkthrough: Blood blockage looks like a clot, but blood belongs to the wordplay; blockage alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban on trade with a country, blocking goods from moving.

clue.text: Soft drink consumed, high in a rooftop structure

indicators.note: something consumed has been taken inside, so it sits within the drink

parts.note: cola is a soft drink
up means high, aloft

explanation.surface: Someone sips a fizzy drink while up on a roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A cupola is a small dome on a roof, a classic rooftop structure.

clue.text: Lawman's modernist tendency in poetry?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the famous Prohibition agent who pursued Al Capone
second meaning: the quality of writing like the modernist poet T. S. Eliot

explanation.surface: A lawman turns out to have a taste for modernist verse.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's means is: the lawman is the answer. Eliot Ness led the Untouchables against Capone; read as Eliot-ness it is a coined word for being like T. S. Eliot, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Eliot Ness was a US federal agent; adding -ness to the poet's surname makes a playful noun for Eliot-like style.

clue.text: Upset to be like 24

indicators.note: upset means turned over, which in a down entry flips the letters upward

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist

explanation.surface: Someone is upset at being compared to another.
explanation.walkthrough: 24 down is SATAN, so like 24 asks for an adjective describing him.
explanation.definitionFit: Satan is the embodiment of wickedness, so something like him is evil.

clue.text: Old Nick took a chair on the outskirts of Austin

parts.note: someone who took a chair sat down

indicators.note: the outskirts of a place are its edges, so only the outermost letters count

parts.note: the first and last letters of Austin

explanation.surface: An old man named Nick rests on a chair at the edge of a Texas city.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Nick looks like an elderly man; it is a traditional nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Nick is a traditional nickname for the Devil.

clue.text: Hesitation at lingerie's shade

parts.note: um is the sound of someone hesitating
a bra is an item of lingerie

explanation.surface: Someone pauses before choosing the colour of their underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Shade is not a colour here but a shadow.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbra is the darkest part of a shadow, such as the full shadow cast during an eclipse.

clue.text: 10 altered briefly

indicators.note: altered means changed, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: the answer to 10 across, MINUS, supplies the letters

explanation.surface: A cross-reference that seems to say the tenth item was changed only a little.
explanation.walkthrough: This pairs with 10 across, whose clue rearranges this answer; each is an anagram of the other.
explanation.definitionFit: In sum is an idiom meaning in short or to summarize, so it matches briefly.

clue.text: Courteous jockeys buy overseas, perhaps

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre and shift about, so the letters change places

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Polite horse riders go shopping abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Jockeys looks like riders but is a verb meaning manoeuvres.
explanation.definitionFit: To outsource is to obtain goods or services from an outside supplier, often a foreign one, hence perhaps.

clue.text: Spies extinct bird after holiday in Pacific islands

indicators.note: after puts the preceding pieces later in the build than the one it names

parts.note: Easter is a spring holiday
the National Security Agency is the US signals-intelligence agency
the moa was a giant flightless bird of New Zealand, now extinct

explanation.surface: Secret agents spot a long-dead bird while vacationing in the South Seas.
explanation.walkthrough: Spies looks like a verb meaning sees, but it is the agency. Eastern Samoa is the older name for the islands now called American Samoa.
explanation.definitionFit: Eastern Samoa is the group of Polynesian islands in the South Pacific that became the US territory of American Samoa.
